This temporary page checks the computational side of the publishing boundary. It combines the
distinct behaviours previously spread across several research fixtures. See [[Markdown Features]]
for the Quartz-rendered half of the system.

```{python}
#| label: computation-setup
#| include: false
import knowledge_theme
import pandas as pd

knowledge_theme.apply()

sample_sizes = [10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000]
errors = [0.25, 0.16, 0.09, 0.06, 0.04, 0.025, 0.018]
summary = pd.DataFrame({"n": sample_sizes, "error": errors})
```

## Python output

For independent samples with finite variance $\sigma^2$, the standard error of the sample mean is

$$
\operatorname{SE}(\bar{X}_n) = \frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{n}}.
$$

The final expression in a Python cell uses Jupyter's rich display system:

```{python}
#| label: computation-table
summary
```

## Static Matplotlib figure

```{python}
#| label: fig-static-convergence
#| fig-cap: Absolute error against sample size on log-log axes.
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fig, axis = plt.subplots()
axis.plot(sample_sizes, errors, marker="o")
axis.set(xscale="log", yscale="log", xlabel="samples", ylabel="absolute error")
plt.show()
```

## Interactive Plotly figure

```{python}
#| label: interactive-plotly
import plotly.express as px

figure = px.line(
    summary,
    x="n",
    y="error",
    markers=True,
    log_x=True,
    log_y=True,
    labels={"n": "samples", "error": "absolute error"},
)
figure
```
